Run an experiment to inspect the firmware's decisions and sensor readings.

Compare identical setups and moving-sampling settings for a fair branch comparison. Every run records the exact source commit.

Native C execution · deterministic hardware model · local only

What this experiment tests

The selected branch's navigation, signal filtering, line search, motor controller, IMU driver, faults, and BLE client are compiled and executed as native C. The car follows actual PWM writes.

Ideal inputs

Equal wheels, no slip, no inertia, no obstacles, deterministic gyro quantisation, successful I²C, constant 100 ms Wi-Fi scans and 100 ms BLE advertisements. Signal follows RSSI = reference − 10n log₁₀(distance), without noise, fading, or antenna effects. Firmware receives integer dBm, so small movements can still produce equal readings.

Model assumptions

Default full-duty wheel speed is 0.76 m/s and wheelbase is 0.14 m; adjust these to your robot. The BLE radius is the assumed distance at −50 dBm, not a measured real-world range. It stays fixed when a branch changes its acceptance threshold. The map circle indicates the selected firmware threshold. The radio model clamps distance below 1 cm and RSSI to −126…−1 dBm.

Coverage boundary

The selected branch supplies both the car firmware and the AP1 beacon firmware. The beacon’s actual startup, advertisements, packet handlers, payload validation, reply bytes and acknowledgements execute. Hardware transport is simulated; the beacon is booted before the car and its idle heartbeat loop is not scheduled. Pico hardware, interrupt timing, the BTstack implementation, flash persistence, and radio coexistence are not emulated. Passing here checks software behaviour under these assumptions; it does not prove the real robot works.

The map's coordinates and distance are ground truth for you. The controller receives no beacon coordinates or distance.

Branch support

Branches must expose a supported getting_there module interface (including main, Alvin and Alvin_2). Unsupported branches are labelled; incompatible code produces a build error, never a substituted algorithm. “Current working tree” snapshots your saved edits. No checkout or source file is changed.

Playback

The native run computes quickly in simulated time. Play, pause, step and scrub inspect that recorded execution. To test a real firmware stop, set the GP21 time and rerun. Saved traces include source identity, car and beacon file paths, settings, measurements and logs.
